rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.
Change only gradient duration to determine whether the tightly clustered early peaks respond to slope. This also tests the resolution margin of the later pair near R = 1.5.

Test a substantial temperature increase against injection 1 to probe selectivity within the unresolved early cluster. Higher temperature should also preserve room under the 10-minute time threshold for subsequent slope refinement.

Retain the favorable high-temperature selectivity and make the gradient shallower to improve the remaining R = 1.14 pair. The last peak should still elute before 10 minutes, potentially reaching the maximum CRF.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so change the starting organic fraction to probe selectivity instead. A modest increase to phi0 should leave the first peak retained while shifting the early cluster.

Increase phi0 one more step to extend the improvement in the remaining critical pair. The first peak should remain above the essentially unretained region, and the run remains comfortably below the time-penalty threshold.

Injection 6 reached the maximum CRF; now shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep the solvent window and temperature fixed to isolate the effect of gradient duration.

Reduce the final organic fraction to make the 8-minute gradient slightly shallower, aiming to restore both marginal pairs to R ≥ 1.5. The last peak previously eluted near phi = 0.64, so phi1 = 0.85 should still keep it within the gradient while improving speed over injection 6.

Test whether one higher starting-organic step can shorten the fully resolved method while preserving the early-cluster separation. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method if early peaks become too compressed.

Test a gradient slope between injections 7 and 8 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary. The narrower window should still accommodate the last peak, while the critical early pairs are expected to remain close to R = 1.5.

Test whether a small temperature reduction rebalances the two marginal early separations at the faster gradient slope. Injection 10 still has a pair below 1.5 despite its rounded CRF, so injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Back off one final-organic step from injection 10 to restore the marginal pair above R = 1.5 while retaining a six-minute programmed gradient. The last peak should elute near the gradient end, with little risk of a prolonged hold.

Test a shallower gradient at phi0 = 0.20 to recover the early pair that fell to R = 1.35 in injection 9. This explores whether the higher starting organic fraction can support full resolution with better separation margins.

With maximum-CRF methods already secured, probe the opposite temperature extreme for a different elution order in the early cluster. The steep, high-ending gradient should keep the last peak within the time threshold while testing an alternative selectivity regime.

Return to the successful high-temperature regime and modestly flatten the gradient relative to injection 8. This should increase the critical-pair resolution margin while keeping all peaks comfortably within 10 minutes.

Flatten the gradient one further step from injection 13 to bring its remaining R = 1.43 pair above 1.5. This tests an alternative fully resolved solvent window with potentially greater critical-pair margins, while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Combine the better early-pair balance at phi0 = 0.15 with a shallower gradient to increase resolution margins. This should retain the maximum CRF with the last peak still below 10 minutes, complementing the faster but marginally resolved injection 8.

Narrow the upper gradient endpoint one step to test a larger critical-pair resolution margin without incurring a time penalty. The last peak in injection 17 eluted near phi = 0.59, so this endpoint should remain sufficient, though the last peak may enter the final hold.

Return toward the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, using an endpoint between injections 8 and 15. This should retain maximum CRF with slightly more separation margin than injection 8 and a shorter elution time than injection 15.

Test the remaining grid point between the fully resolved injection 8 and the faster, marginally unresolved injection 7. This locates the speed boundary directly; retain injection 8 if the critical pair falls below R = 1.5.

Preserve injection 15’s successful gradient slope while ending the ramp two minutes earlier. The early separations should remain fully resolved; this tests whether a brief final hold can retain maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Match injection 8’s fully resolving slope but end the ramp earlier to test a lower-organic final hold. Early resolution should be preserved; the key question is whether the last compound still elutes before the 10-minute penalty threshold.

Use a shallower slope than injection 22 and a higher final organic fraction to improve early-pair margins and reduce hold-related retention. This should preserve maximum CRF while offering a narrower solvent window than the fastest confirmed method, injection 8.

Test the intermediate slope between injections 15 and 17 to retain maximum CRF with a moderate resolution margin and all peaks inside the gradient. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method; this run targets a less marginal alternative.
